Read-only audit. Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Be VERY thorough. Do NOT modify any file.

I need a precise inventory of the CONTENTFUL integration, to plan SFCC-748 "Breadcrumb and SEO – Contentful Component": a new Contentful content type holding category ID (mandatory), title, intro text, expanded SEO body, with locale support — keyed by SFCC category ID so a PLP can fetch its SEO block.

Investigate and report with EXACT absolute file paths:

1. `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — list EVERY file. For each, read it and report: the content type ID, its name, and its full field list (field id, type, required?, localized?, validations). I want a complete table of what content types already exist. Pay special attention to any that already key off a category/SFCC id, and any that already have a "rich text body" or "title + intro + body" shape.
2. `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` and `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — read both. Report: how a new content type gets added to the template (what exactly must a developer edit/add to ship a new type), and what commands run it (`npm run sync:contentful`, `npm run install:contentful`). Report the exact steps needed to add ONE new content type.
3. `overrides/app/components/contentful/` — list every subdirectory and read the key files. Report: how a React component is registered with Contentful (Studio Experiences? `defineComponents`? a registry file?). Show the exact registration pattern with a real example. Where does registration live?
4. Read `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` fully (and useContentful.test.ts skim). Report: the hook's signature, what query options it supports (can it query by an arbitrary field value, e.g. `fields.categoryId=X`?), locale handling, whether it supports `content_type` filtering, and its return shape.
5. Read `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` — report the type definitions present, especially any per-content-type entry types.
6. `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — read it. Report config shape, preview/draft gating, space/environment handling, and LOCALE handling (is locale passed per request?).
7. `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx` and `overrides/app/components/contentful/experienceBySlug/index.tsx` — read both. Report how a Contentful-driven page currently resolves content and renders it. Is there an existing slug->entry pattern that a categoryId->entry pattern would mirror?
8. Check for a rich-text renderer: grep for `@contentful/rich-text-react-renderer`, `documentToReactComponents`, `richText`. Report exact file path(s) of any existing rich-text rendering component (I was told there's a `richText.tsx` somewhere) and what it supports (does it handle links? headings? lists?).
9. Check package.json for all `contentful*` dependencies and their versions.
10. Report the LOCALE story concretely: how do the 11 active locales map to Contentful locales today? grep for locale mapping in the contentful config/hook/scripts. Is localization already wired end-to-end, or is it single-locale today?
11. Check `.docs/integration/` for any Contentful doc (e.g. `NN-contentful.md`) and summarise what it says about adding new content types and about locale.

Report concisely with exact paths. Be blunt about what SFCC-748 would ADD vs. what already exists. Specifically answer: "to ship one new content type, exactly which files change and what commands run?"

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). ############ hooks/useSizeGuide.ts ############
     1	import { useMemo } from 'react';
     2	import { CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE } from '../config/contentful';
     3	import { useContentfulEntries } from './useContentful';
     4	import { pickMostSpecificByRegion } from '../utils/resolveByRegion';
     5	import type { SizeGuideEntry, SizeGuideTableEntry } from '../types/contentful';
     6	
     7	// Narrow-guard used inside useMemo to filter out any sizeGuideTableReference items that
     8	// resolveLinkedAssets could not resolve (e.g. unpublished entries absent from includes.Entry).
     9	const isResolvedTableEntry = (t: unknown): t is SizeGuideTableEntry =>
    10	  typeof t === 'object' && t !== null && 'fields' in t;
    11	
    12	/**
    13	 * Normalises an SFCC `c_sizeGuide` value to a Contentful entry key segment.
    14	 *
    15	 * SFCC stores size guide keys with a trailing numeric variant suffix and hyphens
    16	 * (e.g. `"clothing-op-4"`). Contentful entry keys use underscores and no suffix
    17	 * (e.g. `"clothing_op"`). This function strips the trailing `-{digits}` and
    18	 * converts the remaining hyphens to underscores.
    19	 */
    20	export const normaliseKey = (key: string): string => key.replace(/-\d+$/, '').replace(/-/g, '_');
    21	
    22	/**
    23	 * Resolves a Contentful `sizeGuide` entry for the given SFCC `c_sizeGuide` key and locale,
    24	 * with its `sizeGuideTableReference` links resolved to full `SizeGuideTableEntry` objects.
    25	 *
    26	 * Resolution order:
    27	 * 1. `size-guide__{key}__{locale}` — locale-specific entry (locale = `{language}_{COUNTRY}`)
    28	 * 2. `size-guide__{key}` — default fallback
    29	 * 3. `null` — guide section hidden silently
    30	 *
    31	 * All fields are `localized: false`, so the Contentful fetch always uses
    32	 * `CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE` to avoid unnecessary re-fetches on locale change.
    33	 * The SFCC locale is used only for constructing the locale-specific key.
    34	 *
    35	 * `sizeGuideTableReference` Entry links are resolved inline by `resolveLinkedAssets` via
    36	 * the `include=2` response — no separate sizeGuideTable collection fetch is needed.
    37	 *
    38	 * @returns The matched entry with resolved table references, or `null` when no match is found
    39	 *   or `sizeGuideKey` is absent.
    40	 */
    41	export const useSizeGuide = (
    42	  sizeGuideKey: string | undefined,
    43	  locale: string,
    44	  siteId: string,
    45	): { sizeGuide: SizeGuideEntry | null; isLoading: boolean } => {
    46	  // Compute candidate keys before the fetch so the filter can be passed to Contentful,
    47	  // avoiding an unfiltered full-collection fetch.
    48	  const normalisedKey = sizeGuideKey ? normaliseKey(sizeGuideKey) : undefined;
    49	  // SFCC sends IETF locales with hyphens (e.g. 'en-AU'); Contentful entry keys and
    50	  // locales[] use underscores ('en_AU') per the sizeGuide key regex and locales validation.
    51	  const canonicalLocale = locale.replace('-', '_');
    52	  const localeKey = normalisedKey ? `size-guide__${normalisedKey}__${canonicalLocale}` : undefined;
    53	  const defaultKey = normalisedKey ? `size-guide__${normalisedKey}` : undefined;
    54	  const keyFilter =
    55	    localeKey && defaultKey
    56	      ? `fields.key[in]=${encodeURIComponent(localeKey)},${encodeURIComponent(defaultKey)}&select=sys,fields`
    57	      : undefined;
    58	
    59	  // All sizeGuide fields are localized:false — fetch with fixed locale to avoid re-fetches.
    60	  // Disabled when there is no key so products without a size guide skip the Contentful fetch.
    61	  // sizeGuideTableReference Entry links are resolved inline via include=2 by resolveLinkedAssets.
    62	  // include=3 required: sizeGuide → sizeGuideTable → imageFallback (image entry) → asset
    63	  const { data: entries, isLoading } = useContentfulEntries<SizeGuideEntry>(
    64	    'sizeGuide',
    65	    false,
    66	    CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE,
    67	    keyFilter,
    68	    Boolean(sizeGuideKey),
    69	    3,
    70	  );
    71	
    72	  const sizeGuide = useMemo(() => {
    73	    if (!sizeGuideKey || !entries || !localeKey || !defaultKey) return null;
    74	
    75	    // For each candidate key group, pick the most region-specific entry eligible for
    76	    // siteId. Guides with no regions (or empty regions) are global fallbacks; guides
    77	    // with regions are valid only when a linked RegionEntry.fields.siteId matches.
    78	    const localeMatches = entries.filter((e) => e.fields.key === localeKey);
    79	    const defaultMatches = entries.filter((e) => e.fields.key === defaultKey);
    80	    const matched =
    81	      pickMostSpecificByRegion(localeMatches, siteId) ?? pickMostSpecificByRegion(defaultMatches, siteId) ?? null;
    82	
    83	    if (!matched) return null;
    84	
    85	    // Filter out unresolved links (entries absent from includes.Entry that resolveLinkedAssets
    86	    // could not resolve — they have no `fields` property).
    87	    const resolvedTables = (matched.fields.sizeGuideTableReference ?? []).filter(isResolvedTableEntry);
    88	
    89	    return {
    90	      ...matched,
    91	      fields: {
    92	        ...matched.fields,
    93	        sizeGuideTableReference: resolvedTables,
    94	      },
    95	    };
    96	  }, [entries, sizeGuideKey, localeKey, defaultKey, siteId]);
    97	
    98	  return { sizeGuide, isLoading };
    99	};

############ .docs/integration/02-contentful.md ############
     1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
     2	
     3	## 1. Purpose and scope
     4	
     5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
     6	
     7	In scope:
     8	
     9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
    10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
    11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
    12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
    13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
    14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
    15	
    16	Out of scope of this document:
    17	
    18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
    19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
    20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
    21	
    22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
    23	
    24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
    25	|---|---|---|---|
    26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
    27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
    28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
    29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
    30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
    31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
    32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
    33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
    34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
    35	
    36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
    37	
    38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
    39	
    40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
    41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
    42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
    43	
    44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
    45	
    46	```
    47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
    48	        │
    49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
    50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
    51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
    52	        │
    53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
    54	        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
    55	        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
    56	        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
    57	        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
    58	        │        CPA token is present, both paths fail explicitly with
    59	        │        a 404 and are noindex (no delivery fallback). The Live
    60	        │        Preview SDK requires the token in the browser for
    61	        │        postMessage-based real-time updates.
    62	        │
    63	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
    64	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
    65	        │
    66	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
    67	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
    68	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
    69	```
    70	
    71	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
    72	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
    73	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is set only on dev/test/sit/uat (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
    74	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
    75	
    76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
    77	
    78	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
    79	|---|---|---|
    80	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
    81	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. Both the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages return 404 and are `noindex` when the token is absent — they fail explicitly, with no delivery fallback. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
    82	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
    83	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
    84	
    85	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
    86	
    87	## 5. Data exchanged
    88	
    89	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
    90	|---|---|---|
    91	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
    92	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
    93	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
    94	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
    95	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
    96	
    97	No PII flows through Contentful.
    98	
    99	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
   100	
   101	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
   102	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
   103	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
   104	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
   105	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
   106	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
   107	
   108	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
   109	
   110	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
   111	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
   112	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
   113	
   114	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
   115	
   116	| Failure | Behaviour |
   117	|---|---|
   118	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
   119	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
   120	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
   121	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
   122	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
   123	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
   124	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
   125	
   126	## 9. Security and privacy
   127	
   128	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
   129	- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages, both of which return 404 when no token is present. Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
   130	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
   131	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
   132	
   133	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
   134	
   135	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
   136	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
   137	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.

############ scripts/contentful/README.md ############
     1	# Contentful tooling
     2	
     3	Zimmermann uses **two different Contentful surfaces**. Keep them straight — they live in different places and are managed by different tools.
     4	
     5	## 1. Content types (editorial schemas)
     6	
     7	**What:** Schemas for editorial entries authors fill in (e.g. `footerConfig`, `link`).
     8	**Where:** `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` — plain JS, one file per content type. This is the **sole** source of truth for a content type's fields, including `required`/`localized`/`validations` — there is no separate migration file layered on top.
     9	**How:** Pushed as one organization-scoped **Environment Template**, then installed into each environment. This is Contentful's current recommended mechanism — content models are authored once at the organization level, not created independently per space/environment (see the `contentful-management` SDK's `client.environmentTemplate.*` API).
    10	
    11	```bash
    12	npm run sync:contentful                                   # build/update the template from content-types/*.js
    13	npm run install:contentful -- --target dev                # push it into one environment
    14	npm run install:contentful -- --target dev --dry-run       # validate only, no changes
    15	```
    16	
    17	Driven by [buildTemplate.js](./buildTemplate.js) (assembles `content-types/*.js` into one
    18	`EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`) and
    19	[setup/installTemplate.mjs](./setup/installTemplate.mjs) (validates then installs the
    20	template's current version into `--target <environmentId>`, polling until the install
    21	reaches a terminal status). Reads `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`,
    22	and `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` from `.env`.
    23	
    24	Promotion order: `dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master` — run `install:contentful`
    25	against each target in turn. Contentful tracks each environment's install status/version
    26	natively (`environmentTemplateInstallation`) — there's no hand-rolled migration-history
    27	content type and no separate drift-detection script, since every environment installs
    28	from the same versioned template and can't drift from it the way independently-synced
    29	environments used to.
    30	
    31	**Entries are a separate concern from the template.** Environment Templates cover
    32	content-*type* schema only — seed data (e.g. the canonical `region` entries) needs its
    33	own per-environment script, run after that environment has the relevant content type

    44	per field), then re-run `sync:contentful` followed by `install:contentful` per environment.
    45	
    46	## 2. Studio Experiences component definitions (visual builder)
    47	
    48	**What:** Registers Zimmermann React components with Contentful Studio Experiences so authors can drop them onto pages in the visual builder.
    49	**Where:** `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` — one `.tsx` per component, plus a single generated `definitions.ts` registry.
    50	**How:** Imported at runtime by `defineComponents` — no push step. The registry is **generated from code**; never edit `definitions.ts` by hand.
    51	
    52	### Author workflow
    53	
    54	1. Create or update your component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`.
    55	2. Add `/** @cf-register */` immediately before the component's `const` declaration.

    60	     /** @cf Headline */
    61	     headline: string;
    62	
    63	     /** @cf Hero Image, media */
    64	     heroImage?: string;
    65	
    66	     /** @cf skip */
    67	     internalId?: string;
    68	   };
    69	   ```
    70	
    71	4. Run the generator:
    72	
    73	   ```bash
    74	   npm run generate:contentful
    75	   ```
    76	
    77	   This rewrites `definitions.ts` automatically. Commit both the annotated component and the updated `definitions.ts`.
    78	
    79	5. The pre-commit hook runs the generator automatically when an `experiences/*.tsx` file is staged, keeping `definitions.ts` in sync.
    80	
    81	For full tag syntax and control options, see the `/contentful-register-component` skill.

    84	
    85	```bash

    87	```
    88	
    89	Exits zero if `definitions.ts` is up to date, non-zero (with a diff) if regeneration is needed. Wire into CI to catch a forgotten regenerate.

    92	
    93	- A Studio Experiences component (`experiences/*.tsx`) does **not** belong in [content-types/](./content-types/) — `buildTemplate.js` does not understand it.
    94	- A content-type definition (`content-types/*.js`) does **not** belong in `experiences/` — it is an API artefact, not a runtime component.

# Contentful Component Registration

Studio Experiences definitions are now **generated from code** — you never write a
`defineComponents` entry by hand. The source of truth is the component's `Props` type,
annotated with `@cf` JSDoc tags.

## Steps

### 1. Move the component into `experiences/`

The codegen only processes files under
`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`. If the component isn't there yet,
move it (or create it) in that folder.

### 2. Add `/** @cf-register */` to the component

Place it immediately before the component's `const` declaration:

```tsx
/** @cf-register */
const MyComponent = ({ ... }: MyComponentProps) => { ... };

export default MyComponent;
```

### 3. Annotate every prop in the `Props` type

Props without a `@cf` tag are silently skipped — omitting the tag is how you exclude a prop from the Contentful definition.

```tsx
type MyComponentProps = {
  /** @cf Headline */
  headline: string;

  /** @cf Body Copy, longText */
  body?: string;

  /** @cf Hero Image, media */
  heroImage?: string;

  /** @cf Layout, select */
  layout?: 'left' | 'right';

  internalId?: string;
};
```

**Tag syntax:**

| Tag | Meaning |
|-----|---------|
| `/** @cf Display Name */` | Infer control from the TS type (see table below) |
| `/** @cf Display Name, control */` | Override the inferred control |

Props without any `@cf` tag are silently skipped — no tag needed to exclude a prop.

**Type → control inference table:**

| TypeScript type | Inferred control | Contentful variable type |
|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| `string` | `shortText` | Text |
| `boolean` | `toggle` | Boolean |
| `number` | `number` | Number |
| string literal union (`'a' \| 'b'`) | `select` | Text |

**Valid explicit controls:** `shortText`, `longText`, `select`, `toggle`, `number`, `media`

**Auto-skipped:** props starting with `on` (event handlers), `children` (emits
`children: true` on the component registration instead), and any prop with no `@cf` tag.

### 4. Run the generator

npm run generate:contentful

Answers to your specific questions:
- **`content_type` filtering: yes.** `useContentfulEntries` builds `content_type=${contentType}` and appends `&${filter}` when provided (line 219).
- **Arbitrary field filtering: yes, and already in production use.** The `filter` param is passed through verbatim as Contentful Search Parameters. `fields.categoryId=X` would work today with **zero hook changes**.
